QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_30

question.text: In the context of AIF risk measurement, Standard Deviation primarily measures:

answer.text: Expected return over the risk-free rate
The beta of the portfolio versus a benchmark
Volatility of historical returns from the mean return — a proxy for total historical risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.6.1: Standard Deviation measures volatility of historical returns from the mean — used as a proxy for total (systematic + unsystematic) historical risk. The Trap: Option A is Sharpe numerator concept. Option B is beta definition. Option D is wrong — SD captures TOTAL risk, beta captures systematic only. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B covers SD for Cat III funds; XXI-B uses SD extensively; XV (Research Analyst) similar. Manager's Pro-Tip: For AIFs with <5 years of track record, SD is noisy — supplement with peer-group comparison and stress scenarios. Report SD only on annualised net returns to avoid scaling confusion.
